thread.title: Kyshawn George reflects on NBA growth after Rising Stars win
thread.title_full: Kyshawn George reflects on NBA growth after Rising Stars win

author: j. s. fields
title: Kyshawn George reflects on NBA growth after Rising Stars win
text:
Kyshawn George, a forward for the Washington Wizards, discussed his progress in the NBA and recent experiences at All-Star Weekend, according to a March 10 report. George, who played his rookie season last year, set several records with the Wizards but was not invited to the Rising Stars event during his first year.
George said he used that omission as motivation. “I won’t say I was disappointed,” George said. “But also, I knew internally that I was better than most of the players that were there, so I just kind of doubled down on the work that I did. I didn’t change much, ultimately, but I just made sure that I kept doing what I needed to do. I trusted the work that I was putting in every single day and it just made me realize that you can’t wait for stuff to be given to you. You have to go get it yourself.”
This season marked a change for George as he participated in the Rising Stars tournament in Inglewood, California. He joined teammates Bub Carrington, Tre Johnson and Alex Sarr on Team Vince and helped secure a 25-24 victory over Team Melo. Reflecting on the experience, George said: “I mean, at the end of the day, you’re playing a basketball game. You have new teammates for one night and you just have to go out there and I think you have to compete. I think you have to treat it with respect, and I think that’s what we went out there and did. So, to be able to actually come out with a win, it just makes everything so much better.”
George is currently recovering from an elbow injury expected to keep him out of Tuesday’s game against Miami but has improved his performance this season with averages of 14.8 points, 5.1 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game compared to last year’s numbers.
He credited increased confidence and experience for his development: “Definitely a lot,” George responded when asked how much he’s improved since his playing days at Miami. “Especially in the physicality of the NBA game… The shooting has always been there… But defensively… just being able to guard some of the best players early in my career… your game is going to evolve.” He added that learning from veterans like Kareem Abdul-Jabbar during All-Star Weekend contributed further.
Looking ahead, George expressed goals for both himself and his team: “I’ve always been a hard worker… as long as I keep doing that… there’s no reason why I won’t be playing in many Sunday games.” He also shared enthusiasm about following his alma mater Miami’s progress in upcoming tournaments.
